Photograph: Ukrinform/Shutterstock Russia-Ukraine war at a glance Russia Explainer Ukraine war briefing: Zelenskyy warns Egypt of food supply threat caused by Russian strikes in Black Sea Kyiv says exports to Egypt under threat from Russian attacks; Moscow dismisses idea of Black Sea ceasefire. What we know on day 1,635 Guardian staff and agencies Fri 14 Aug 2026 21.53 EDT Last modified on Fri 14 Aug 2026 23.19 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy has warned Egyptian counterpart Abdel ⁠Fattah al-Sisi of possible food supply shortages caused by Russian strikes on ⁠cargo vessels in the Black Sea . “Ukraine is one of ⁠the largest food suppliers to ​Egypt and to ‌a significant number ‌of other countries in Africa ‌and the Middle East. These supplies are now under serious threat because of Russia’s war,” Zelenskyy said on X. “We are already seeing ‌a significant reduction in supplies, and this could have very ​unpleasant consequences due to rising prices and shortages,” he said, adding that the two countries had agreed to ⁠work on solutions. Russia on Friday dismissed the idea of a ceasefire ‌with Ukraine in the Black Sea , saying it saw no grounds for “half-measures” that would ​offer a respite to the other side. In a statement, foreign ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova accused Ukraine of “brazen acts of terrorism” against shipping, while making no ⁠mention of Russia’s own attacks. “We view these attacks (by Ukraine) as a ​deliberate policy aimed at destabilising civilian ‌shipping in the Black ‌Sea region,” Zakharova said. “At the same time, we see no signs of improvement in the situation and, consequently, no grounds for half-measures that merely grant the Kyiv regime a temporary breathing space.” Both Russia and Ukraine have stepped up attacks in recent weeks against commercial ships in the ​Black Sea, driving world grain prices higher. Zakharova’s comments followed an earlier Ukraine proposal for both sides to halt their attacks on civilian ships in the Black Sea in an apparent attempt to reopen a crucial grain corridor. Kyiv is said to have made the offer through a third party. Russia has intensified its online disinformation campaign in Poland , using a dispute between Warsaw and Kyiv over second world war massacres ⁠to inflame tensions between Ukraine and ⁠its key ally, Polish ​officials and researchers say. The messaging, mostly posted on social media accounts in Polish, also tries to foment anger in Poland against refugees, as opinion polls show support for the far-right growing ahead of closely contested ⁠parliamentary elections in 2027. The long-running second world war dispute between Poland and Ukraine centres on the Volhynia massacres , in which Poland says Ukrainians killed about 100,000 Poles between 1943 and 1945. The dispute intensified after ⁠Zelenskyy named an army unit after insurgents who perpetrated the massacres, prompting hard-right president Karol Nawrocki to strip his Ukrainian counterpart of a top Polish ​honour in June. Russian authorities acknowledged Friday that some regions face new petrol shortages, as Ukraine continues to attack the country’s oil refineries to blunt Russia’s capacity to pursue the war. Russia has shut down one big refinery at Orsk – about 1,300km (810 miles) from the frontline – for six months after it was attacked this week. “The situation remains tense in several regions of the country regarding fuel supplies to service stations,” the government said in a social media post. Oil companies are “taking the necessary measures to increase deliveries to the most vulnerable regions”, it said. Russian jet-powered drones have struck a home in northern Ukraine, killing a 29-year-old woman and her 9-year-old son . This attack comes after the United Nations reported that July was the deadliest month for Ukrainian civilians since the early weeks of Russia’s invasion. At least 437 civilians were killed and 2,610 wounded last month. Meanwhile, Ukrainian drones have targeted Russian infrastructure, including a major port north of Moscow. Romania found ⁠a second drone in national ⁠territory on ⁠Friday , ​in the south-eastern village ⁠of Plauru near the Danube border with ⁠Ukraine, the defence ​ministry said ‌on ‌Friday, after a ‌low flying drone undetected by radar systems crashed earlier. The ministry did not specify ‌the origins of the drone. ​The Nato state has seen Russian drones repeatedly breach ⁠its airspace over the ​last four ​years. Russian president Vladimir Putin told North Korean ⁠leader Kim Jong-un that Moscow and Pyongyang were cooperating across all areas to ensure ⁠regional ​security and stability, North Korean state media KCNA reported on Saturday. Putin said in a message ⁠to Kim marking the anniversary of Korea’s liberation from Japanese colonial rule that he was confident Russia and ⁠North Korea would continue “constructive joint work” on bilateral and international ​issues, KCNA said. Kim had ‌visited Pyongyang’s Liberation ‌Tower on Friday to pay tribute to Soviet soldiers who fought ‌Japan in the second world war, KCNA reported. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/clyx.text: Image source, NurPhoto via Getty Images Image caption, Jewel Howard-Taylor served as vice-president of Liberia from 2018 to 2024 By Makuochi Okafor ,Â BBC Africa Â and Â Harry Sekulich Published 20 August 2026, 04:07 BST Updated 1 hour ago Liberia has charged former Vice-President Jewel Howard-Taylor with drug trafficking, money laundering and a range of other offences as part of an investigation into an alleged transnational narcotics network. She was detained on Wednesday before being able to board a flight at Roberts International Airport in the capital, Monrovia, the country's justice ministry confirmed. Police chief Gregory Coleman has linked her to the seizure last month of cocaine valued at $317m (Â£233m). The 63-year-old politician has yet to make any public comment about the allegations. Her lawyer told the BBC he could not comment until Howard-Taylor was formally charged in court. Howard-Taylor went into politics after her now ex-husband, former President Charles Taylor, left power. He was a former rebel leader who was elected Liberia's president in 1997, remaining in office until 2003. Charles Taylor was later arrested and convicted by a UN-back court of aiding and abetting rebels in neighbouring Sierra Leone during the 1991-2002 civil war, in which some 50,000 people died. Several years later, George Weah picked Howard-Taylor as his running mate and she served as his deputy during his presidency from 2018 until 2024. Cocaine worth $317m seized in Liberia's biggest-ever drugs bust Published 23 July Howard-Tayor faces charges including the unlicensed importation, sale and transportation of controlled drugs, illicit trafficking, criminal solicitation and criminal facilitation. Police have charged three foreign nationals - two Croatians and one Ukrainian - in absentia as part of their investigation. They are accused of being part of the same network as the former politician. Liberian Justice Minister Oswald Tweh said the authorities would use domestic and international measures to locate and arrest them. Liberia has stepped up a crackdown on cocaine trafficking, following two major seizures in June and July. Almost four tonnes of cocaine believed to be bound for Europe were found during the raid in July. The authorities described it as Liberia's biggest drug bust and said it had uncovered a sophisticated transnational trafficking network. The investigation has since extended to senior figures within Liberia's security establishment. The government says its investigations are aimed at identifying not only those directly involved in transporting drugs, but also financiers, organisers and people accused of helping to protect the operation. "No office is too high, no political connection is too powerful, no nationality provides immunity, and no individual is beyond the reach of the law," it said in a statement. West Africa has increasingly been used as a major transit route for cocaine trading from South America to Europe, with traffickers exploiting porous borders and weak enforcement in parts of the region. https://www.bristolpost.co.uk/whats-on/s.text: A trip to the beauty salon is a luxury many of us enjoy, yet the costs can quickly mount up. The alternative of a DIY home manicure often falls short, lacking the durability and polished finish of a professional treatment. However, shoppers are increasingly abandoning their salon appointments in favour of a mineral bond nail set from Australian brand Sistaco – and the retailer is currently offering a deal where beauty enthusiasts can receive three additional colours completely free of charge. Usually priced at £100.95, the set is currently available for £75, roughly equivalent to the cost of two salon gel manicures. The set utilises a mineral bond applicator to deliver non-toxic, HEMA and TPO free results in the comfort of your own home. The brand guarantees buyers 'salon results at home from the first application' and claims the system can be removed effortlessly in just minutes. Those who dread waiting for their nails to dry will be delighted to learn that this manicure dries instantly, eliminating the risk of smudging for the less careful among us. The set has the potential to save frequent salon visitors hundreds, if not thousands, of pounds on their fortnightly appointments. Users simply apply a base coat and set it with an LED light, dust the powder onto the nail, apply a thin layer of top coat, and finish by setting the look under the LED light once more, reports OK! . Should the Sistaco set not appeal, LookFantastic is currently stocking the Mylee The Midi Gel Polish Kit (worth £122) for £59.25 , reduced from £79, featuring an LED lamp, four bestselling gel polishes and more. For those seeking nail care essentials, Sephora's £19.99 Manicure Tool Kit could be worth considering. The set includes a nail clipper, nail file, cuticle pusher, and cuticle nipper. Returning to Sistaco, the brand's Mineral Bond Nail Set has achieved an impressive 4.8 star rating out of five on the retailer's website. The brand has also garnered strong reviews on Trustpilot, where customers have awarded the company 4.5 out of five stars based on thousands of reviews. One satisfied customer commented: "Those compliments keep coming. I find in restaurants or cafes the girls/ladies that serve me always compliment my nails. Seems random strangers can't resist! They're always so impressed when I say I did them myself." Another said: "Is this some sort of magic? Love this kit and how easy it is to do at home and long lasting. Just past the two week mark on the first mani and still going strong." A third wrote: "Goodbye to salons! This is 1 week+ and going strong. This system is so easy, convenient. I'm in love with the time and money savings. Thank you Sistaco - 10 stars." However, one reviewer did mention experiencing some difficulty with the home application process, noting: "As a right handed novice doing my left hand was really easy, the right not so easy. I'm sure as I get more practice my right hand will get a lot better, I also love the colour." Nevertheless, one satisfied customer praised the durability of the products in a Trustpilot review, writing: "Sistaco is BY FAR the best system/polish that I have ever tried! I am also very conscious of toxins and love that this is non toxic!" "I also love that it last at least two weeks and can handle all the cooking, cleaning, hand washing, and childcare activities I do as a working mom!" A further reviewer on the platform commented: "Sistaco is spectacular. I've tried basic polish, gel, and dip powders, but nothing compares to Sistaco. I was hesitant to try yet another system, but I am so glad I did. "It's easy to apply, long‐lasting, and gentle on my nails. The colours are gorgeous, the products are high‐quality, and the community is incredibly friendly and supportive. I very highly recommend Sistaco Mineral Bond nail products." Shop the Mineral Bond Nail System on the Sistaco website.

https://www.atvtoday.co.uk/315543-travel.text: Christmas is coming early to Vilnius, with the Lithuanian capital already confirming its plans for the 2026 festive season While plenty of European destinations are still keeping their Christmas plans under wraps, Vilnius has already given travellers something to look forward to. The Lithuanian capital’s festive season will officially begin on 28 November 2026 , when its famous Christmas tree is switched on, while the Vilnius Christmas Market will run from 28 November until 27 December . The early announcement comes as travellers increasingly look beyond Europe’s biggest festive destinations for quieter Christmas breaks. According to Skyscanner’s 2026 report, 34% of travellers are seeking less crowded destinations , while 32% say overcrowding negatively affects the quality of their holidays. And with major Christmas attractions continuing to attract millions of visitors, Vilnius is positioning itself as an alternative for those who want the festive atmosphere without quite so much elbow-bashing. “For us, Christmas isn’t about ticking off attractions – it’s about traditions,” said Eglė Girdzijauskaitė, Head of Communication at Go Vilnius. “It’s meeting friends at the Christmas Market, choosing handmade gifts from local artisans, or crafting Baltic scented candles together. “Locals love escaping the winter cold in a traditional sauna and taking time to enjoy the festive atmosphere. That’s the kind of Christmas we invite visitors to experience in Vilnius.” Vilnius’ famous Christmas tree returns The centrepiece of the celebrations will once again be the Vilnius Christmas Tree , although exactly what it will look like remains a closely guarded secret. The annual unveiling has become one of the city’s most anticipated festive moments, with designers creating a different artistic interpretation of the tree every year. Past designs have included fairy tales, birthday cakes, clocks and more traditional red-and-gold Christmas themes. The city’s trees have also regularly featured in international rankings of Europe’s best Christmas trees, having been named the most beautiful Christmas tree in Europe for four consecutive years . In 2025, Vilnius was also named the European Capital of Christmas , recognising the city’s festive traditions and its increasingly celebrated Christmas displays. The tree lighting on 28 November will officially launch this year’s celebrations. Christmas Market returns to Cathedral Square Following the tree lighting, the Vilnius Christmas Market will take over Cathedral Square from 28 November to 27 December . The market is set beneath the giant Christmas tree, with last year’s edition featuring 48 wooden huts arranged in a promenade-style layout. Visitors can expect local food and drink, including gingerbread, colourful sweets and mulled wine, alongside handmade gifts from Lithuanian artists and artisans. Among the potential finds are scented candles, amber jewellery and traditional wooden toys. The market is just one part of Vilnius’ wider Christmas programme. The city’s UNESCO-listed Old Town is transformed with thousands of lights and decorations, while previous festive seasons have featured an open-air ice rink in Town Hall Square, a traditional two-storey carousel and a Christmas train winding through the illuminated streets. A quieter alternative to Europe’s busiest Christmas markets? Vilnius’ pitch is increasingly centred around experiencing Christmas rather than simply visiting Christmas attractions. The city offers traditional sauna experiences, including at Ivanas Muša Gongą and the Beer Spa, alongside boutique accommodation such as Bokšto SPA. There are also Michelin-recognised restaurants, independent artisan shops and the atmospheric Old Town to explore between festive activities. And for visitors lucky enough to encounter snow, the historic centre can provide a particularly picturesque backdrop to the Christmas celebrations. The Vilnius Christmas Tree Lighting takes place on 28 November 2026, with the Christmas Market running from 28 November to 27 December 2026. https://www.globalsecurity.org/wmd/libra.text: Military WMD Menu Introduction Systems Facilities Agencies Operations Countries Hot Documents News Reports Policy Budget Congress Links Intelligence Homeland Security Space Weapons of Mass Destruction (WMD) Iliana Iotova: The Conflict in Ukraine Has No Military Solution President of the Republic of Bulgaria 4 September 2026 | 16:34 Head of State meets with the Prime Minister of Slovakia The conflict in Ukraine has no military solution and must end as soon as possible, and this is the responsibility of every country in the European Union. Diplomacy and negotiations are needed. This was stated by President Iliana Iotova at a meeting with the Prime Minister of Slovakia Robert Fico, who is visiting our country. There are very few politicians in the European Union who talk about peace as much as you and the Bulgarian Prime Minister, Fico said in turn. The head of state welcomed the Slovak Prime Minister in the Coat of Arms Hall at Dondukov 2. The two held a one-on-one meeting, after which talks between the Bulgarian and Slovak delegations took place. Iotova highlighted the excellent development of relations between Bulgaria and Slovakia in all spheres of cooperation, as well as the good interaction of the two countries within the framework of the European Union. The Bulgarian head of state and the Slovak prime minister also discussed the EU's Multiannual Financial Framework. Bulgaria and Slovakia share common positions on the cohesion and Common Agricultural Policy, which was emphasised during the conversation. According to President Iotova, during the negotiations on the EU's Multiannual Financial Framework, it is necessary to intensify cooperation within the Friends of Cohesion group. The desire of the European institutions to vote on it as soon as possible, without clearing up problematic aspects of it, creates risks for the competitiveness of some countries, she added. Iliana Iotova and Robert Fico also discussed the enlargement of the European Union. They were adamant that the accession process should be according to the rules and based on the achievements of the candidate countries. You know that we have certain problems with the Republic of North Macedonia and its membership in the EU. We are looking for your support for Skopje to follow the European accession policy. For four years, we have not seen progress in the implementation of the commitments undertaken by the Republic of North Macedonia in 2022," the president noted. The President highlighted the care of the Slovak side for the Bulgarian community, its cultural and educational institutions. This is extremely important for us, Iotova pointed out and added that the 80th anniversary of the founding of the Bulgarian Secondary School "Hristo Botev" in Bratislava is coming soon. In connection with cooperation in the field of education, she also highlighted the Bulgarian language lecturers at leading universities in Slovakia.

https://www.politico.eu/article/europe-b.text: The United Kingdom, Germany and Poland have reaffirmed their support for Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy after U.S. President Donald Trump said the country needed a new leader . Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk wrote on X that he was “absolutely convinced” nobody could break Ukraine and its president in their “fight against Russian aggression.” “I have assured [Zelenskyy] that he can count on Poland’s and Europe’s full solidarity with the Ukrainian nation,” he added. Advertisement Advertisement German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul also reaffirmed his country’s support for Zelenskyy Sunday, while calling for greater pressure on Moscow to return to peace talks. “We need continued consistency and clarity on the side of Ukraine,” he told Reuters at a meeting of the governing Christian Democrats. The show of support comes after Zelenskyy and Trump traded barbs Saturday following Washington’s decision to ease diesel sanctions on Russia . “I think it’s time for Ukraine to get a new president,” Trump told reporters at the White House as he criticized Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil facilities. On Sunday, the Ukrainian president stated on social media that his country would be prepared to stop attacking Russian oil refineries “if Russia stops striking our energy infrastructure.” The U.K. also reiterated its support for Kyiv following Trump’s remarks. “We stand with Ukraine. We stand with President Zelenskyy,” British Defense Secretary Wes Streeting told the BBC Sunday morning, adding that Ukrainians alone should decide who leads their country. Streeting said Russian President Vladimir Putin started the war and could end it, and added that Britain’s priority would be to seek reconciliation between Kyiv and Washington. On Saturday, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham spoke with Zelenskyy and reiterated Britain’s “complete solidarity,” Downing Street said. Burnham acknowledged that “the last 24 hours had been difficult for Ukraine” and pledged to strengthen sanctions, according to the statement. Advertisement Advertisement

https://aa.com.tr/en/europe/explainer-po.text: Europe EXPLAINER - Police deployed after head of top court suspended, president cuts trip short: What's happening in Poland? 'At such a moment, the President must be in Poland. I'm interrupting my flight to Senegal. I'm returning,' says Karol Nawrocki Burak Bir 31 October 2026 • Update : 31 October 2026 LONDON 'This is a difficult process, sometimes painful, and it requires decisive action. There is no other way,' says Prime Minister Donald Tusk Polish envoy to China resigns following developments, says he 'can no longer serve' Polish President Karol Nawrocki cut short a trip to Senegal on Friday to return to Warsaw as riot police were deployed to the top court and its president was suspended amid an escalating constitutional crisis. The crisis surrounding Poland's top court, the Constitutional Tribunal, escalated after the government suspended its two senior justices and moved to bring criminal charges against them. Prime Minister Donald Tusk's government and Nawrocki have been locked in a dispute over the tribunal's composition. Judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska issued orders suspending Tribunal President Bogdan Swieczkowski and Vice President Bartlomiej Sochanski from their duties. Korwin-Piotrowska accused the leadership of obstructing the work of judges elected by the parliamentary majority, violating judicial procedures and preventing the proper functioning of the tribunal. But the tribunal rejected the orders, saying on its website that Swieczkowski "remains the president of the Constitutional Tribunal and Sochanski remains the vice president." It wrote on US social media company X: "All persons participating in these actions are committing the crime of a coup d'état." Following the announcement, protesters gathered outside the tribunal building as tensions escalated, with some reportedly climbing over the fence and throwing objects at police. Reactions Following the developments, Nawrocki said he was cutting short his trip to Senegal and returning to Poland. "At such a moment, the President must be in Poland," he wrote on X. Tusk said: "Restoring the rule of law is our duty." "After years of PiS (party)-led lawlessness, this is a difficult process, sometimes painful, and it requires decisive action. There is no other way," he added. Meanwhile, Polish Ambassador to China Jakub Kumoch resigned following the developments. "In light of the events in the country, I have concluded that it is no longer possible for me to continue serving as the Ambassador of the Republic of Poland. As of today, I have submitted my resignation and a request for recall," he wrote on X. Police said they had not entered the court building and denied claims that officers had stormed it. Law and Justice (PiS) party leader Jaroslaw Kaczynski and other opposition politicians arrived outside the court and accused the government of trying to seize control of the institution. Kaczynski described the events as a "coup against the Constitutional Tribunal" and urged Nawrocki to intervene. Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski, in the US city of Atlanta for a G20 meeting, said measures concerning the Constitutional Tribunal aimed to restore the court's functioning after "politicization under the previous government." Long-running legal dispute The crisis began after the PiS-led government took office in 2015, as the PiS majority in parliament quickly moved to appoint judges to the court to gain a majority, since the court can decide the legality of legislation. The European Court of Human Rights and the Court of Justice of the European Union ruled that the PiS majority had improperly elected three judges because they duplicated positions that the previous parliament had validly filled. The European courts ruled that Poland's Constitutional Tribunal was no longer an "independent and impartial tribunal." Tusk's government has used the rulings as a basis to stop publishing the tribunal's rulings. When he took office in 2023, Tusk vowed to depoliticize the judiciary, but he partially failed because Nawrocki and his predecessor, Andrzej Duda, used their presidential vetoes to block the attempts. PiS and Nawrocki accused the government of using the rule-of-law campaign to remove political opponents from key state institutions. Nawrocki was expected in Warsaw late Friday evening as the standoff continued and was set to meet the first president of the Supreme Court, Zbigniew Kapinski. news_share news_share_description subscription_contact subscription contact_the_ombudsman is_there_an_error_in_this_story ombudsman_apply_button LATEST NEWS All US accuses Iran of threatening maritime security, demands accountability at UN UN warns of rising maritime attacks, urges restoration of safe navigation in Strait of Hormuz, Red Sea US stocks close mixed as tech losses weigh on Nasdaq, Europe mostly up Türkiye publishes law approving ratification of Mecca joint defense pact London police investigate British author David Walliams over alleged sexual offenses International Criminal Court closes original Afghanistan war crimes investigation Nationwide ground stop issued at US airports over 'communication issue': Transport secretary See All Polish foreign minister defends police action at Constitutional Tribunal amid political dispute China's Xi urges stronger cooperation with Europe
